slides.headline: Whoopi Goldberg worked as a bricklayer
slides.body: In the 1970s, Goldberg moved to San Diego, then to Berkeley. She worked odd jobs there, including as a bank teller, a mortuary cosmetologist, and a bricklayer.

photo.query: bricklayer hands laying bricks construction Wikimedia Commons
photo.prompt: close-up of hands laying red bricks with mortar on a construction site, sharp detail, dramatic side light

slides.headline: She also worked with a theater troupe
slides.body: Goldberg joined the avant-garde theater troupe the Blake Street Hawkeyes. She also gave comedy and acting classes in Berkeley.

photo.prompt: small theater stage with a single spotlight, empty seats, and a rehearsal feel

slides.headline: Mike Nichols helped move her show to Broadway
slides.body: She created The Spook Show in 1983. Nichols saw her perform and helped transfer it to Broadway as Whoopi Goldberg.

photo.prompt: Broadway theater marquee at night with bright lights and a city sidewalk, no readable fake text

slides.headline: The recording won a Grammy
slides.body: The Broadway show ran from October 24, 1984, to March 10, 1985. Its recording won Best Comedy Album, and Goldberg became the first Black female comedian to win a Grammy.
